label: Lyme disease
name: Lyme disease
definition: The survey asks whether a clinician diagnosed Lyme disease; a code means ICD-10-CM A69.2. Self-reporters told the All of Us survey a clinician diagnosed them and they get visits or treatment for it.

summary.population: lyme: current self-reporters, 5 or more years of records
summary.text: of people who report Lyme disease and get care for it have a code for it in their record (95% CI 34% to 45%).
Within the same health systems, women and men who report Lyme disease are coded about equally often (women to men 0.81, 95% CI 0.57 to 1.13).
Tick or insect bite codes are 17.1 times as common in the year before a first Lyme disease code as in matched people without Lyme disease.

layers.label: Reported cases (CDC)
layers.title: Average yearly Lyme disease cases per 100,000 residents, 2015 to 2019
layers.takeaway: 15 states and the District of Columbia average 10 or more reported cases per 100,000 residents a year, CDC's threshold for high incidence, led by Vermont (135) and Maine (121).

source.text: CDC National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System (confirmed and probable cases) and US Census Bureau population estimates, average of 2015 to 2019.

counties.note: State spread: CDC withheld the county count, and the state's withheld cases were spread per capita over its counties without a published row.

layers.label: Share coded (All of Us)
layers.title: Share of people who report Lyme disease who have a code, by state
layers.takeaway: In the 2 states with enough participants, 50% (Massachusetts) to 67% (Pennsylvania) of people who report Lyme disease have a code for it, against 39% for all participants who report it.
